reviews.author: Lola M.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful location, went on a Monday so my group was mostly alone for the time we were there. Arrived and went to the Tongue Point when the tide was going back out and this opened up lots of tide pools. Got to see some diverse wildlife like invertebrates, birds, and fish. We took my seven year old nephew and he was able to climb up and down the rocks but with help. If you have kids I would be aware it might be difficult to get down to the water if they are younger but still doable depending on the tide!! As with any tide pools be careful where you step, there were barnacles, anemone and mussels all over the rocks, I’d recommend water shoes :)

reviews.author: Stephaine W.
reviews.text: Great place to go camping and spending time with your loved ones. I love how much nature and the smell of sea waking up!! It’s a must go!! So many places to see and check out for days!! Netting new people!

reviews.author: Paldi P.
reviews.text: Tons of parking and fee free during the winter.  So many camp sites with awesome views and nice bathrooms.  Nice playground and easy walkabout.  You can access the rocks and the sea but it’s down stairs and hiking the rocks.  Not for young kids or faint of heart.  Tons of campgrounds above the sea with amazing views.  There is extra parking with a few overnight.

reviews.author: P T.
reviews.text: We spent several months living in Port Angeles and ended up spending more time here playing than any other single spot. It was fun to beach comb, watch sunsets, play in the water or the park. Something for everyone and not too crowded.

reviews.author: Joshua D.
reviews.text: Salt Creek is honestly a PNW Paradise.  It’s where the lush green forest literally tumbles right into the beautiful blue sea. You can spend hours wandering through the old WWII bunkers hidden in the woods, then head down to the fingers below the bluff to find some of the most vibrant tide pools you’ll ever see, teeming with life. It’s one of those rare spots where history and the raw beauty of the coast just perfectly collide. You have to make sure to wander out onto the sand beach at the mouth of the creek too! If you catch the tide low enough, you can actually walk all the way out to the island to explore.

reviews.author: amanda
reviews.title: Not to be missed, rain or shine!
reviews.text: As locals, we're here all the time, and it's not to be missed, rain or shine! We try to camp at least once a year, with reservations if we're lucky, and we visit multiple times a month. The tide pools are always filled with friendly crabs, along with anemones and the occasional starfish! (((Please don't remove any of our beloved critters; leave them for everyone to enjoy))) The kids love holding the various crabs, and we always make sure to return them to their hiding spots ;) We frequently see seals and otters, but whales are possible; be mindful of the information boards, which provide important information and potential warnings for the area! The battlements are a short hike (or drive) away, and are an interesting part of history! The view of Crescent Bay is awesome, and there is a huge field perfect for picnics. There is also a playground and bathrooms near the entrance, as well as a few bathrooms throughout the campground.

reviews.author: Julie J
reviews.title: Fun and interesting.
reviews.text: Definitely a place to visit during low tide. The tide pools were amazing. We arrived on an unexpectedly warm May Day, the crowds were abundant but so were the Tide pools. A great first day entering the Olympic National Park.

reviews.author: hiker_rich
reviews.title: Not so clean anymore
reviews.text: I have been going to Salt Creek for 5 years. It's a great site. The campers are peaceful. It's clean -- or at least was until this year. The bathrooms, except for the vault toilet, are fine. The big rig sites in the open may be fine. But all 3 of the smaller sites in the trees that I looked at had litter. Including an abandoned sock at one. Sad to see.

reviews.author: Marz0-vd
reviews.text: There are trash that are left everywhere by people who come here. Slippery rocks littered with plastic.

reviews.author: EKeane
reviews.title: worth a visit
reviews.text: Well worth the 20-25 minute drive from Port Angeles. It's a beautiful shoreline and there are lots of tide pools with sea creatures (anenome, crabs, etc). If you drive through the camping area, there are a few places along the way to park and walk down to the shore. Make sure to wear gym shoes because you'll have to scale over rocks/boulders to get to the tide pools.

reviews.author: MissMK43
reviews.text: Not enough bathroom facilities for the campers it can hold. Staff was great and very accommodating to our large group. They helped us find a spot as this is a first come first service camp ground. But they made sure to help us out even though there were booked solid. They checked books and registrations and found that a few campers had not shown up or called and after 24 hour they make that space available. They were happy to help us.

reviews.author: Anne S
reviews.text: Salt Creek Recreational Area offers lovely views of the Straits of Juan d'Fuca and British Columbia. The tide pools are spectacular but not to be enjoyed by children without supervision. Walking & hiking paths acre interesting and offer all levels of expertise. One walk takes you to a bit of WWII History & you can find fun mounts that guarded the Straits. There are trailer sites available but be sure to make your reservations early as they fill up fast, especially in the summer. There are clean, but few bathrooms for the amount of visitors. A community building is available by reservation for a nominal fee. A great place to visit anytime of year! Don't miss "Salt Creek Rectional Area" on your next visit to the Olympic Peninsula.

reviews.author: Diane O
reviews.text: Went to go tide pooling but they were not very impressive. Pretty park to hike around and would be really nice to camp at. The campsites were very nice and the hosts were as well.

reviews.author: Kaylee A
reviews.text: Honestly, one of the best campgrounds I've ever been to. Self check in at the bulletin board, they take all forms of payments even tap to pay. $45/night for residents and $55/night for non-residents. The kiosk prints a ticket that you keep in your windshield. The gates to the campground close at 9pm, which means you can't come or go after that time. Bathrooms, dump station, dumpsters, fire pit, picnic tables. This place has it all and the views are unbelievable. *there's also free day use for anyone, including your vehicle and/or rigs!

reviews.author: Sandy V
reviews.text: An absolute gem of a campground. I 100% recommend staying here, and more than one night! They do have a reservation system but if needed, also offers a good amount of first come first served sites. The hosts were on point and making sure the area was safe. We had a miscommunication regarding our site for the 1st night but the hosts helped clear it up and we went on our merry way. We kayaked, hiked, biked, and enjoyed the beautiful scenery. We saw eagles, all kinds of marine life, it was amazing 👏

reviews.author: Jaiden F
reviews.text: The grounds are absolutely beautiful especially during sunset. Each camping lot is decently close to another but it still feels pretty secluded due to the trees and nature surrounding each lot.
